transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you here?

Well, I came in because things have been a bit off lately. Ever since my father-in-law moved in with us, I just... I haven't really been myself. I’ve been holding it together at work alright, but at home and with my coursework, I’m a lot more wound up and short-tempered than I’m used to being. 

And I’ve started skipping the things that usually keep my head clear. I haven't been going fishing, I dropped my woodworking projects, and I even stopped going to the first-aid workshops I usually like to attend. I just wanted to talk to someone to figure out how to get a handle on it.
Have you been feeling sad or down most of the day?
No, I wouldn't really say I feel sad. I'm not down in the dumps or anything like that. It's... well, it's really just the frustration and being wound up, like I mentioned. But no, I don't feel sad.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about many different areas of your life, rather than mainly about your father-in-law living with you?

No, I wouldn't say that. I'm not really a worrier in general. My job is fine, and I'm not stressing over finances or my health or anything like that. It's really just... well, it all comes back to the situation at home with my father-in-law. That's what's got me so wound up, not everything else.
When did you first start feeling this wound up and irritable in relation to your father-in-law moving in?

Well, he moved in about four months ago. I'd say I started noticing the strain within the first couple of months. It just kind of built up once the new home routines and the day-to-day caregiving demands really settled in as our new normal. That's when I realized I was getting so on edge.
How much has feeling wound up and irritable interfered with your daily functioning at home or with your coursework?

Well, I'm still doing my EMT work just fine, so that hasn't been affected. But... I have fallen behind on some of my paramedic coursework. It's just hard to focus when I'm this tense. And I've also stopped showing up consistently for the community first-aid workshops I usually help out with. I just don't have the patience for it right now.
